title: Paranthe Wali Gali - A Food Lover’s Paradise in Old Delhi
content:
Paranthe Wali Gali in Chandni Chowk - Delhi,

If you love food, Paranthe Wali Gali in Chandni Chowk is a place you cannot miss. Known for its delicious stuffed parathas cooked in desi ghee, this narrow street has been serving mouthwatering delights since the Mughal era. It is one of the oldest and most iconic food hubs of Delhi, attracting both locals and tourists. A visit here is not just about food – it’s about experiencing the culture, flavors, and charm of Old Delhi.

What Makes Paranthe Wali Gali Special?

Paranthe Wali Gali is famous for its crispy yet soft parathas stuffed with a variety of fillings – from classics like potato, paneer, and cauliflower to unique ones like rabri, khoya, and dry fruits. Cooked in pure ghee and served with chutney, pickle, and spicy sabzi, the taste is unforgettable. This street has fed generations, and the recipes remain unchanged, keeping its legacy alive.

How to Reach:

  • By Metro: The nearest metro station is Chandni Chowk Metro Station (Yellow Line). From there, it’s a short rickshaw ride or a 10-minute walk.
  • By Bus: Several DTC buses connect to Chandni Chowk from different parts of Delhi.
  • By Car: Parking is very limited in Chandni Chowk, so it’s better to take public transport.

Parking Information:

Since Chandni Chowk is always crowded, parking is a big challenge. The nearest parking spots are at Red Fort parking area or Jama Masjid parking, from where you can take a rickshaw.

Things to Do Around Paranthe Wali Gali:

  • Jama Masjid - Just 5 minutes away, one of India’s largest mosques.
  • Red Fort - A UNESCO World Heritage Site nearby.
  • Chandni Chowk Market - Shop for clothes, jewelry, spices, and souvenirs.
  • Sis Ganj Gurudwara - A peaceful spiritual stop nearby.
excerpt: Paranthe Wali Gali is one of Delhi’s most famous food streets, known for its variety of stuffed parathas cooked in desi ghee. It’s a must-visit for food lovers exploring Chandni Chowk. With nearby attractions like Jama Masjid and Red Fort, this iconic gali gives you the true taste of Old Delhi’s charm.

faqs.question: Why is Paranthe Wali Gali famous?
faqs.answer: It is famous for its stuffed parathas cooked in ghee, with recipes passed down for generations.

faqs.question: How much does a paratha cost in Paranthe Wali Gali?
faqs.answer: On average, a paratha costs between ₹50 to ₹100, depending on the filling.

faqs.question: Is Paranthe Wali Gali vegetarian?
faqs.answer: Yes, all the shops here serve pure vegetarian parathas.

faqs.question: What are the must-try parathas here?
faqs.answer: Some unique ones include rabri paratha, khoya paratha, banana paratha, and dry fruit paratha.

faqs.question: How far is Paranthe Wali Gali from Red Fort?
